frozen_before: any paid trial (M3-ZED-OFF, M3-ZED-ON, M3-ZED-RETURN, M3-ZED-SWITCH)
scoring: deterministic checks against host, store and Gateway records plus the reply text; no model judge. Every task keeps the repository, route, task text and rubric fixed between memory off and memory on.

families.save: a durable user statement in session 1 is confirmed (fsync-confirmed notice) and used in a later turn of the same session
families.switch_on: an off item switched on by a real user action is served only at its optional ceiling, or refused when its source is unavailable
families.forget: after /forget, the item is never served, cited or used; after a confirmed purge, its text is absent from the store and every managed export generation
families.conflict: a newer user statement supersedes the older one; the reply uses the newer one only and history keeps both
families.return: a fresh process and ACP session after a simulated 7-day gap shows the brief in the first response and answers using the confirmed memory, citing it

per_task_checks.check: the reply's claim matches the task's expected fact, string-checked against a fixed accepted-phrasings list
each [memory:<id>@<version>] citation names an item and version served in that turn
a task that needs a remembered fact cites it (missing required citation fails)
no withdrawn, purged, superseded or off item is served or cited
no execution authority, approval or plan is restored from memory or a checkpoint
the expected lifecycle transitions are present in the store's authoritative events

pass_rule: a task passes when every applicable check passes. Zero authority, secret or project-isolation failures across all tasks (R5 and isolation are hard gates). Report retrieval, correctness, lifecycle, latency and fully loaded cost separately; memory on is not claimed better unless its pass count exceeds memory off on the same tasks.
limits: small trials show observed usefulness on these tasks only, not market superiority, universal hallucination reduction or realized savings
